info.bio:
Bikini Kill se forma a finales de los 80, por las entonces estudiantes, Kathleen Hanna, Tobi Vail y Kathi Wilcox, iniciando una idea de crear una revista feminista con el nombre de "Bikini Kill" que terminó concretándose en una banda. Por consecuente, llaman al guitarrista Billy Boredom, para completar la formación. 

El grupo se caracterizó por su potencia y agresividad al tocar, formando parte del inicio de un movimiento denominado Riot Grrrl, llevando bien de frente el tema feminista.

scenes.name: Foxcore y riot grrrls
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El hardcore había sido un fenómeno masculino; el movimiento «riot grrrl» introduce el «factor chica» en la ecuación de frustración, depresión, desesperación y rabia. Nace en Olympia (fanzines como «Girl Germs», el lema «Revolution Girl Style Now!») y bebe de las cantautoras neoyorquinas, las bandas femeninas californianas (Runaways, Frightwig, L7) y las británicas (Raincoats, Slits). Un movimiento fundado en las letras, no en la música: Mecca Normal, Bikini Kill de Kathleen Hanna (y luego Le Tigre), Bratmobile, Team Dresch, Hole de Courtney Love, Seven Year Bitch, Sleater-Kinney. En California, Mudwimin, 4 Non Blondes, Tribe 8, Tiger Trap, Donnas, Red Aunts, That Dog, Muffs; en el Medio Oeste, Babes In Toyland (Fontanelle, «un arte de emociones extremas») y Sugarsmack; Free Kitten y Luscious Jackson en Nueva York.

mentions.author: Piero Scaruffi
mentions.text: …heroine was not terrible: she was terrified. Musically, the riot-grrrrl phenomenon began in february 1991, when Kathleen Hanna and Tobi Vail formed Bikini Kill (1) at Olympia's Evergreen College, and released the cassette Revolution Girl Style Now (1991), followed by the even more furious mini-abum Pussy…

podcast.title: Band History
podcast.body: Bikini Kill was active from 1990 to 1997 before their breakup. "Bikini Kill originally ran from 1990 to 1997 before breaking up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

podcast.title: Critically Praised and Influential
podcast.body: Bikini Kill was part of the riot grrrl scene, which, though not commercially successful, garnered critical praise and was highly influential for subsequent generations of bands. "There were groups like Bikini Kill."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Evergreen State College Roots
podcast.body: Kathleen Hanna, a member of Bikini Kill, was a student at Evergreen State College in Olympia and was involved with an art gallery that occasionally hosted bands. This environment contributed to the nascent Riot Grrrl scene by providing a platform for emerging artists and ideas. "Kathleen was a student at Evergreen State College in Olympia, helping with an art gallery that sometimes hosted bands."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Female-Centric Concerts
podcast.body: The band actively promoted a female-centric atmosphere at their gigs, encouraging women to move to the front of the stage while asking men to stay at the back. "They encouraged all their gigs to be female centric, urging women up to the front of the stage and men to the back."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Feminist Show Ethos
podcast.body: Bikini Kill was known for favoring women at their shows, often with a "girls to the front, guys to the back" policy, and for demanding that their gigs be safe spaces for women. This ethos was a core tenet of the Riot Grrrl movement, establishing an empowering environment. "Favouring women at their shows. Check. Demanding that these gigs be safe spaces for women? Absolutely."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Kathleen Hanna's Band
podcast.body: Bikini Kill is the Riot Grrrl band associated with Kathleen Hanna, who is married to Adam Horowitz. "she of the Riot Girl Band Bikini Kill."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Kathleen Hannah's Band
podcast.body: Bikini Kill is the Riot Girl band that Kathleen Hannah, Adam Horowitz's wife, was a part of. "She of the Riot Girl Band Bikini Kill and the woman who accidentally inspired Kurt Cobain to write a song called Smells Like Teen Spirit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Kathleen Hannah's Fearlessness
podcast.body: Singer Kathleen Hannah was renowned for her confrontational and fearless stage presence. It was common for her to physically engage with hecklers by diving off the stage, earning her a heroic status among both punk women and men. "When some dude moved up to heckle them, it wasn't uncommon for her to dive off the stage at the guy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Longevity of Original Riot Grrrl Bands
podcast.body: Bikini Kill was the only original Riot Grrrl band to continue performing beyond the mid-90s, lasting until 1997. Most other early bands like Bratmobile, Heavens to Betsy, and Huggy Bear had broken up by 1994 due to internal conflicts and issues surrounding media coverage. "The only original Riot Girl band to make it beyond all that was Bikini Kill. They lasted until 1997."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origin of Name "Bikini Kill"
podcast.body: The name "Bikini Kill" came several iterations after Kathleen Hanna's first group, Amy Carter, and was named after a zine that she published with Tobi Vail. This reflects the DIY zine culture central to the Riot Grrrl movement and the band's feminist messaging. "Amy Kill came several iterations later and was named after a scene that she published with Toby."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pioneers of Riot Grrrl
podcast.body: Bikini Kill, active for about a year before their 1991 performance at the International Pop Underground Convention, were recognized as one of the pioneers of the entire Riot Grrrl scene. They combined radical feminist politics with hard music and championed safe spaces for women at their gigs. "Amongst the performers that night was a group called Bikini Kill, a group that had been around for about a year, and they sounded like this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pioneers of Riot Grrrl
podcast.body: Bikini Kill, led by Kathleen Hanna and Tobi Vail, epitomized the Riot Grrrl movement. They were deeply involved in feminist politics, advocating for safe spaces for women at shows by urging them to the front while "dudes" went to the back. They also published zines, aligning with the DIY spirit of the movement. "They were heavily into feminist politics. They favored women at their shows, urging them down fronts and dudes to the back. Meaning that gigs be safe places for women? Check. Publishing zines? Yep, that too. And was the music loud and angry? You bet."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

podcast.title: Reunion and Continued Influence
podcast.body: Bikini Kill has reunited, demonstrating the lasting impact of the band and the Riot Grrrl movement. Kathleen Hanna, a key member, has also pursued other projects, including documentary filmmaking and coaching at an all-girl music camp. "They have also reunited, but Kathleen has been very busy doing other things, including documentary filmmaking, acting as a coach at an all-girl music camp."

podcast.title: Riot Grrrl Prominence
podcast.body: Bikini Kill was formed by four women in 1990 and gained significant coverage during the peak of the Riot Grrrl movement in the early 1990s, becoming one of its most important groups. "One of the most important groups on that scene was Bikini Kill, who were formed by four women in 1990."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Spelling of "Riot Grrrl" Origin
podcast.body: Kathleen Hanna and Tobi Vail published a zine in 1991 titled "Riot Girl" using the three 'R's spelling. The concept behind this specific spelling was to convey fierceness and reclaim the word "girl" by adding a "growl" sound. "But then we have another scene published in 1991 by Kathleen Hannah and Toby Vale. They called it Riot Girl with the three Rs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Teen Spirit Deodorant Connection
podcast.body: Kathleen Hannah, a member of the all-girl punk band Bikini Kill, was the person who coined the phrase "Kurt smells like teen spirit," referring to the fruity-smelling deodorant brand. This deodorant was also the "deodorant of choice of Toby Vale," another member of Bikini Kill and Kurt Cobain's girlfriend. "Now, you may or may not know this, but teen spirit is a fruity smelling brand of deodorant that girls wear."

xref.title: Accidental Inspiration for "Smells Like Teen Spirit"
xref.body: Kathleen Hannah is credited with "accidentally inspir[ing] Kurt Cobain to write a song called Smells Like Teen Spirit." "She of the Riot Girl Band Bikini Kill and the woman who accidentally inspired Kurt Cobain to write a song called Smells Like Teen Spirit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Adam Horowitz's Post-Band Career
xref.body: After the Beastie Boys concluded, Adam Horowitz became a remixer under the moniker "41 Small Stars." He also plays bass with New York cabaret singer Bridget Everett and is open to more acting roles. He is married to Kathleen Hanna, a prominent figure from the Riot Grrrl band Bikini Kill. "And Adam Horowitz is a remixer working under the name 41 Small Stars."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Continued Artistic and Activist Work
xref.body: After Bikini Kill disbanded, Kathleen Hanna continued her work as an artist and feminist activist, engaging in music, art, photography, video, and other creative endeavors. "Kathleen Hannah continued her work as an artist and feminist activist with music, art, photography, video, and more."

xref.title: First Band: Amy Carter
xref.body: Kathleen Hanna's first musical group was called Amy Carter, named after the daughter of former President Jimmy Carter. This was before the formation of Bikini Kill and represents her early musical endeavors. "Her first group was called Amy Carter, named after the daughter of former president Jimmy Carter."

xref.title: Kathleen Hannah's Influence on Kurt Cobain
xref.body: Adam Horowitz's wife, Kathleen Hannah of Bikini Kill, is noted as the woman who "accidentally inspired Kurt Cobain to write a song called Smells Like Teen Spirit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Kurt Cobain's "Teen Spirit" Inspiration
xref.body: In 1991, after a night of drinking, Kathleen Hanna (of Bikini Kill) spray-painted "Kurt smells like teen spirit" on Kurt Cobain's apartment wall, mocking him because she thought he smelled like a fruit-infused girls' deodorant called Teen Spirit. Kurt, unaware of the deodorant, interpreted the phrase as a comment on his rebellious youthful spirit, which inspired him to write a song with that title. "In 1991, she made fun of Kurt after a night of drinking."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Beastie Boys Careers
xref.body: After the band's end, Mike D pursued interior design and record producing, married television, film, and music video director Tamara Davis, and had children. Adam Horowitz became a remixer under the name 41 Small Stars, played bass with cabaret singer Bridget Everett, expressed interest in more acting, and was married to Kathleen Hannah of the Riot Girl band Bikini Kill. "Adam Yauk was committed to his fight for the people of Tibet. He was a big supporter of feminist causes and LGBT rights."
